Product design · Design system · Developer handoff

EraTrade Platform

A prop-trading platform where traders were leaving before they paid. I redesigned the product for desktop and mobile, built its design system and handed it to development.

Role
Product designer
Scope
Desktop and mobile, English and Russian
Year
2026
Delivered
Figma library, working prototype, developer handoff

Where users were lost

Users opened the challenge purchase and many never reached payment. I went through the live platform screen by screen and found four causes.

1

No sense of progress

Two unlabelled circles were the only progress indicator.

2

Price before explanation

The total sat above the table that described what it covered.

3

Payment looked optional

"Expand" was a solid button. "Pay" was grey text beside it.

4

Statuses looked alike

"Awaiting stage 1" and "Awaiting payment" differed only by the colour of a dot.

A system that holds across screens

Violet marks an action and nothing else. Green appears only on money a trader has already earned. The same row, card, tab and status components carry every screen.

Clearer navigation

The original sidebar held twelve items in one list, including two internal links visible to every trader. I grouped it by how often each place is opened and pinned the account to the bottom.

Before · the original platform
After · my redesign
Hover and click the items
1

Grouped by use

Seven places a trader works in, then three reference links.

2

A place to land

The platform opens on an overview of the account, not a purchase form.

3

Account at the bottom

Name and UID stay visible without using a navigation slot.

4

Internal links removed

Admin and Manager were visible to every trader. They no longer appear.

A purchase that reads in order

Buying a challenge

Configuration, total and payment method now share one screen. The total updates as the trader chooses, and the conditions table sits directly beneath it.

Challenges list

The challenges screen follows the same logic. Unpaid challenges lead with payment, and active ones open straight to the login and password.

Designed for the phone

The mobile version is built around checking progress. The sidebar became a bottom bar with the places traders return to, the purchase sits in the middle as a single button, and rule tables became stacked rows.

Tournament page in three states

The tournament page changes with the trader's situation: before joining, while competing and after the results are in. Each state shows only what matters at that moment.
